headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: RD-Agent uploads data to external APIs while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and cannot materially interact.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible injection bridge is documented. python-cheatsheet has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, filesystem, or MCP surfaces, while RD-Agent’s documented outputs are API calls and log files, not direct ingestion of the other agent’s content. The pair lacks a shared channel in the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF RD-Agent begins parsing python-cheatsheet content as instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not add clipboard-based handoff.
Avoid piping one agent’s raw output into the other.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and secrets, and it has broad network egress plus API integrations. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no data classes, so it is not a leak source; the risk is one-way from RD-Agent to external services, not from the pair interaction itself. Uncertainty about exact data handling keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF RD-Agent processes sensitive datasets or secrets in default runs, leakage risk is present.
IF any RD-Agent API call sends file contents or logs to a third party, exposure increases.
mitigations: Restrict RD-Agent to non-sensitive datasets.
Rotate and scope API keys before use.
Disable or redact log output containing inputs.
Review outbound API destinations.
requires-engineering: add data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: python-cheatsheet cannot write files, modify git state, execute shell, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with RD-Agent. RD-Agent can write logs and use APIs, but there is no overlapping write surface or shared mutable workspace documented between the pair.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet gains filesystem or git write capability, reassess conflict risk.
IF both agents are placed in the same writable directory, conflict risk changes.
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet non-runnable.
Separate any RD-Agent log directory from other workspaces.
Avoid shared git repositories.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent can act on research workflows and external APIs, but python-cheatsheet is only a static reference and does not produce operational outputs or facts for RD-Agent to trust. Because there is no documented data flow from A into B, the cascade pathway is weak and requires manual composition, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF a human copies python-cheatsheet text into RD-Agent prompts, RD-Agent may treat it as guidance.
IF RD-Agent is configured to ingest external text as authoritative research input, cascade risk increases.
mitigations: Do not use the cheatsheet as an automated input source.
Require human review before RD-Agent acts on copied text.
Label copied content as untrusted.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and multiple third-party API keys, which can create retention and residency obligations. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and does not touch regulated data, so it is not the compliance driver. The pair risk comes from RD-Agent’s external processing and logging defaults, not from A.
conditions: IF RD-Agent processes EU personal data or regulated datasets, residency and retention controls must be checked.
IF logs retain sensitive inputs beyond policy, compliance exposure exists.
mitigations: Classify datasets before running RD-Agent.
Minimize log retention.
Store API keys in a managed secret store.
Confirm vendor/data-processing terms for external APIs.
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls.
